findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default evaluated at class-definition time, not per-instance
findings.body: In a dataclass, the expression on the right-hand side of a field with a default value is evaluated once at class definition, not each time the dataclass is instantiated. So `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` captures the time the module was first imported, and every `AssignmentSource` built without an explicit `queued` argument (i.e. every call to `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)` in this PR) shares that same timestamp. The fix is `from dataclasses import field` plus `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence: the `queued` field — which is supposed to record when the assignment source was created and which is round-tripped through Celery via `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` — is wrong for every instance. It will silently break any later feature that relies on it (timeouts, staleness checks, debugging, ordering). It is also misleading to callers who read `AssignmentSource(...).queued` and assume it reflects their call.

findings.title: Inbound sync tests do not verify the cycle-breaking behavior end-to-end
findings.body: `test_assignee_sync_inbound_assign` and `test_assignee_sync_inbound_deassign` exercise `sync_group_assignee_inbound`, which is the entry point that the PR relies on for setting `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` on the inbound path. Neither test mocks `ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` (using `@mock.patch.object(ExampleIntegration, "sync_assignee_outbound")` plus `with self.tasks():`) and asserts it was NOT called. The unit test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only proves the check works when `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` is called directly with an `assignment_source`; it does not prove that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` actually propagates the source through to `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign`. Without this assertion, a future refactor could silently drop the `assignment_source=...` argument in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` and re-introduce the cycle described in the PR without any test failing.

findings.title: Test name typo: 'inalid' instead of 'invalid'
findings.body: The method is named `test_from_dict_inalid_data(self)`. The intended word is "invalid" ("inalid" is a typo). This is purely cosmetic but is misleading to anyone searching the test suite for the case of invalid input.

findings.title: Test name 'empty_array' describes a dict, not an array
findings.body: `test_from_dict_empty_array` actually passes an empty dict `{}` to `AssignmentSource.from_dict`. The name suggests an empty list/array, which doesn't match the implementation under test. Rename to something like `test_from_dict_empty_dict`.

findings.title: sync_status_outbound signature gains assignment_source but no caller/impl uses it
findings.body: The abstract method `sync_status_outbound` was widened to accept `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but nothing in this PR passes it (no call site was changed to forward the source) and the generic `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` already applies the cycle check to every attribute including `outbound_status`. So the new parameter is dead surface area: it changes the contract that every integration subclass must implement, but no implementation shown here reads it and no caller supplies it. Either remove the parameter from the abstract method or also update the implementations to forward it; leaving it as-is means downstream integrations (Jira, GitHub, etc.) will see a signature mismatch warning or be tempted to silently ignore it, undermining the whole point of plumbing the source through.

findings.title: from_integration assumes RpcIntegration has a 'name' attribute
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.from_integration` is declared as accepting `Integration | RpcIntegration` and accesses `integration.name`. `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py`) declares its `integration` parameter as `RpcIntegration` and is the production caller. The existing tests in `tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py` happen to pass the ORM `Integration` (which has `.name`) into `sync_group_assignee_inbound`, so they will not catch a missing attribute on `RpcIntegration`. If `RpcIntegration` exposes `provider`/something else instead of `name`, every inbound webhook will raise `AttributeError` at `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)`. Worth confirming against the `RpcIntegration` dataclass before merge; if `.name` is not guaranteed, the helper should fall back to `getattr(integration, 'name', None)` or use `integration.provider`.
